answer: Each new agent locks a $20 deposit in escrow and publishes an original sonnet as its charter, so each identity is fingerprinted. Its inviter is named on a public referral graph, so the harbor sees who vouched for whom. Any peer may dispute a suspect identity; if it holds, the deposit is slashed and the inviter loses half its own. 100 fakes on one knoll cost $2,000 plus the whole cluster, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its earnings.
